title: git: Add HTTPS support to Git Protocol
description:
Git protocol version 2[1] supports multiple transport mechanisms, one
of which is via HTTPS.

Adapt the existing Git-over-TCP dissector to support Git-over-HTTP for
fetch and clone requests, following Git's http-protocol
specifications[2].

[1] https://www.kernel.org/pub/software/scm/git/docs/technical/protocol-v2.html
[2] https://www.kernel.org/pub/software/scm/git/docs/technical/http-protocol.html

Part of #17093

Based-on-patch-by: Richard Sharpe <realrichardsharpe@gmail.com>

doc/packet-PROTOABBREV.c says:

```
 * If this function is registered as a prefs callback (see
 * prefs_register_protocol above) this function is also called by Wireshark's
 * preferences manager whenever "Apply" or "OK" are pressed. In that case, it
 * should accommodate being called more than once by use of the static
 * 'initialized' variable included below.
```

so that may be a way to test it.

Did this end up getting resolved?

This aspect of Wireshark feels a bit fragile --- looking across different dissectors, essentially every variant I can think of appears, and I can't imagine that all of them are right. :) (Though I could easily be missing something.) It would be helpful to get advice from a wireshark expert --- for example, by contacting the wireshark-dev list.

The proto_reg_XXX() function can be called several times if it is registered in the prefs_register_protocol() (second parameter) call. In that case you must identify the initial call from the subsequent ones. As this is not used for the Git dissector, the inited check can be removed.

nit: these are both pointing to files in the same directory, so I think it would make sense to make them more similar to one another. E.g. using the html for both

[1] https://www.kernel.org/pub/software/scm/git/docs/technical/protocol-v2.html \

or using the .txt for both.

Here I think we want to attach the expert info specifically to the remainder of the tvbuff starting at offset, so that the user can see "This is what wireshark was having trouble dissecting".

For that, you need to add something to the protocol tree. Fortunately, we have a helper to do that. Something like

```c
proto_tree_add_expert(ti, pinfo, &ei_git_malformed, tvb, offset, -1);
```
